messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — the int8 canary we rolled for raven-mini on dedicated is showing a small but consistent uptick in funcall parse failures (~1.7% -> 3.9% overall on canary slice). latency looks good (median down ~18%), cost per token ~2.3x lower, but JSON parse errors spike on longer tool outputs.
Mira: interesting — is the failure correlated with seq len or batching? any example payloads?
Alex: failing mostly when output length > 600 tokens, and when we enable aggressive batching (batch size 24). attaching one raw assistant chunk below:

Chen: ```
..."result": {"action": "create_task", "args": {"title": "Q2 run", "notes": "started at 2026-02-...
(unexpected EOF)
```

Chen: looks truncated — closing brace missing, so our strict JSON parser rejects. sometimes there's a stray unicode byte sequence near the end in the token stream.
Sam: could be streaming cutoff or kv-cache eviction leading to early EOS. Did runtime log an EOS token or stream closed?
Alex: runtime shows normal EOS for float16 baseline. for int8 canary, half of these failures are "stream end without EOS" in the serve logs. here's a grep sample: `grep -E "stream_end|eos|client_disconnect" canary-logs-2026-04-28.log` -> several stream_end entries right after last token batch.
Jules: notable difference in kernel scheduling? int8 path might flush partial buffer if last batch smaller than continuous batch granularity. cc eng-runtime.
Mira: quick triage plan: 1) run single-threaded canary with batching disabled for same prompts to confirm batching interaction; 2) increase max_output_tokens and add a small delay before closing the stream to let final tokens arrive; 3) add a soft-parse fallback that attempts closure heuristics (append missing braces/brackets) and reparse once before marking a funcall failure. thoughts?
Chen: +1 on closure heuristics but keep it behind flag and instrument. propose heuristic: if top-level JSON parse fails and last char != '}' -> try appending up to 4 closing braces/brackets and attempt parse. also try inserting a `"_incomplete": true` sentinel when we patch so evals know patched vs clean.
Sam: prefer fixing at runtime if possible — keep heuristic as rescue only. I'll open a kernel issue for the int8 flush behavior and run microbench to reproduce with synthetic long outputs.
Alex: ran a quick A/B today: no-batching int8 slice dropped parse failures back to 1.9% (still higher than float16 baseline 0.5%). so batching exacerbates but doesn't fully explain.
Jules: for evals, let's create a dedicated telemetry slice: sample 10k funcalls across lengths (100/400/800/1200) and record fields: model_variant, batch_size, stream_closed_by, parse_status, patched_flag, latency. add these to the canary dashboard + alert if patched_flag rate > 0.5% over 3h.
Mira: agree. also add a quality metric: downstream tool acceptance rate (did the external tool accept the args after patch). that will tell us if our repair is safe.
Oncall-bot: [incident] funcall-parse-rescue-rate exceeded threshold on canary at 1724990182. Alert routed to #eng-ml-oncall.
Alex: thanks — I can own the telemetry slice + the quick rescue implementation behind a config. will start a PR with tests using trimmed and truncated outputs. pushing plan: kernel probe (Sam), telemetry slice (Alex/Mira), soft patch rescue (Alex), and runtime flush mitigation (Sam). target: two-day canary window.
Mira: perfect. please thread PR link in this channel when ready. also tag @eng-runtime and @eng-oncall in the PR. :thumbsup:
Alex: will do. updating the runbook with the interim mitigation steps now.
